_note: Mints the node the Uganda no-node-yet lead was waiting on: KCCA's own Auditor-General financial-statements report cites 'Section 49 of the Public Finance Management Act' as its preparation basis. The Act's real consolidated text (ULII/Laws.Africa) was fetched and confirmed to exist with Section 49 present (titled 'Audit committees'). CAVEAT left honest rather than silently smoothed over: Section 49 as enacted concerns audit-committee oversight duties, not financial-statement preparation requirements per se -- Section 51 ('Annual accounts') is a closer substantive match to the AG opinion's phrasing. oag.go.ug was unreachable this round (connection reset, not a robots block) so the exact section number as printed in KCCA's own report could not be independently re-verified against a fresh fetch; the basis quote is carried over from the prior round that minted ug-kcca-financial-statements-2024 itself (and therefore presumably read the report directly at that time). The edge represents what that source document states about itself, regardless of whether the auditor's own internal cross-reference is perfectly precise.

reports.title: Public Finance Management Act, 2015 (Act 3 of 2015)
reports.description: Uganda's principal public-finance-management statute, governing budgeting, accounting, audit committees and annual accounts for central government votes and local governments.

dependencies.basis: The Auditor-General's opinion states KCCA's financial statements were prepared in accordance with Section 49 of the Public Finance Management Act.
